content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Finality is the point of civil procedure. Section 10 (res sub judice) stays a later suit while the same matter is pending between the same parties in a competent court. Section 11 (res judicata) bars a later suit after the matter was heard and finally decided.

Why this is asked
Res judicata is a foundational battleground in civil litigation. The critical issues center on the six mandatory conditions and constructive res judicata under Explanation IV.

Essentials of s. 11
1. A former suit.
2. Decided by a competent court.
3. Same parties or persons claiming under them.
4. Matter directly and substantially in issue in both suits.
5. Heard and finally decided.
6. Check Explanations I–VIII. Explanation IV is constructive res judicata: a ground that might and ought to have been raised is treated as decided.

Illustration that works
A sues B for title to a plot and loses after trial. A files a second title suit on the same facts. s. 11 bars it.

Illustration that fails
The first suit was dismissed for default. There is no final decision on merits. s. 11 does not apply (Order IX may).

s. 10 distinguished
Pending twin suit → stay. Decided twin suit → bar. Order II r. 2 is a different bar (relinquished claim from the same cause of action).

Authority
Hope Plantations Ltd. v. Taluk Land Board (1999) 5 SCC 590 — finality.
State of U.P. v. Nawab Hussain AIR 1977 SC 1680 — constructive res judicata.
Workmen v. Board of Trustees, Cochin Port Trust AIR 1978 SC 1283 — Expl. IV.

Current law
Cite ss. 10 and 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

questionsAndAnswers.question: State the conditions of res judicata. How does s. 10 differ?
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. s. 11 CPC bars re-trial of a matter heard and finally decided between the same parties by a competent court.

Essentials. Former suit; competent court; same parties or privies; matter directly and substantially in issue; heard and finally decided; Explanations I–VIII.

Distinction. s. 10 stays a pending twin suit. s. 11 bars a decided twin suit.

Illustration. Title lost after trial cannot be sued again.

Authority. Hope Plantations (1999); Nawab Hussain AIR 1977 SC 1680.

Conclusion. Cite s. 11 CPC, 1908.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain res judicata and constructive res judicata with a problem.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Set out the foundational essentials. Then add Explanation IV: a ground that might and ought to have been made a ground of attack or defence is deemed to have been decided. Apply IRAC to the facts. Distinguish Order II r. 2 (relinquished relief from the same cause of action). Close with ss. 10 and 11 CPC, 1908.
